name: earth_effective_temperature
title: Approximate temperature of the Earth
summary: Sun-Earth-space radiation resistance network: view factors from the disc-to-sphere geometry give the Sun-to-Earth and Earth-to-space resistances; the steady-state heat rate fixes the blackbody emissive power of the Earth and its effective temperature (6.3 °C = 279.4 K).

origin.notes: Example 10.3-3 of Nellis & Klein, Heat Transfer (Cambridge University Press, 2009); EES example (c) F-Chart Software, MIT via EES-Community/ees-examples. The binary .eez companion (EES 11.912) carries the stored solution used as verification reference. Original download page in the file header: https://fchartsoftware.com/ees/examples/examples_heat_transfer_2009/chapter%2010/example%2010.3-3%20approximate%20temperature%20of%20the%20earth.eez

verification.summary: Compared with the EES solution stored in the .eez companion of the source file (19 common variables with --ees-units): 0 differ at rtol 0.001; maximum relative difference 2.5e-7 on the sigma*T^4 quantities (EES stores the Stefan-Boltzmann constant with slightly different last digits), all others to 2.4e-9. T_2 recomputed by hand from the stored E_b_2: 279.44342 K against the stored 279.44344 K.
verification.reference: EES stored solution (22 variables) of the .eez companion ees-examples-raw/uncategorized/example_10.3-3_approximate_temperature_of_the_earth.eez (EES 11.912), compared with tools/compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: Tool summary: '19 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 2; only in CoolSolve: 5' (Only in EES reference: T_2C, T_2F). The two only-in-EES variables are the Fahrenheit and deg.C output conversions of the original, dropped by the card decision; the five only-in-CoolSolve variables are pi, sigma# and the absolute-temperature helpers T_1_K, T_2_K, T_3_K.

history.action: added (T-IMPORT card C-519, candidate EEX-012 of the ees_examples inventory); verified against the EES stored solution of the .eez companion
